A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MS-GODE research, with readable methods, equations, experimental tables, figures, and complete appendices. Renamed concepts and relocated illustrations can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting experiments on simulated physics and biological cellular systems, including comparative results, mask-selection and dropout studies, and performance matrices.

after.justification: v2 retains original physics and cellular forecasting experiments in Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–6, including revised performance-matrix results.

M1.justification: The fixed-weight backbone, system-specific binary masks, ELBO/edge-popup training, and observation-reconstruction mask selection remain unchanged. Splitting mask learning and mode switching into separate subsections reorganizes existing components. Appendix A.1.4 proposes possible future enhancements without implementing them.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same three physics sequences and EGFR1 → Ran1 → EGFR2 → Ran2 cellular sequence. Bio-CDL names the existing biological benchmark. Newly listed variables elaborate previously mentioned variable selection; the phase-transition illustration and prospective benchmark expansion are not additional evaluations.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain Fine-tune, EWC, GEM, LwF, BCMR, SDP, and Joint training. Newly discussed related methods are not added to these comparisons. Appendix A.3 newly discloses manual SDP parameter selection but does not establish a change from the earlier implementation.

E3.justification: The reported sequence configurations, 60/40 forecasting split, training/test sample counts, model dimensions, 20-epoch training, and MSE-based evaluation remain unchanged. Added initialization, task-boundary, and command-line details document existing experiments rather than establish revised protocols.

E4.justification: Figure 6 revises the performance-matrix evidence used to examine forgetting and adaptation across tasks. The mask-binarization, dropout, and sequence-configuration studies are retained. Appendix A.1.4 adds discussion and proposed remedies, without new ablations or robustness experiments.

E5.justification: Both versions report five repetitions with means and standard deviations. v2 additionally supplies an example execution command with --fix_random_seed False, adding seed-handling documentation without establishing additional runs or a changed uncertainty estimator.

E6.justification: Figure 6 substantially replaces the eight reported performance matrices, beyond changing their color scales. For example, the final-task cell in MS-GODE panel (e) changes from the highest displayed error to among the lowest, and EWC panel (f) changes its taskwise error pattern. Tables 1–2 and Figures 4–5 retain their results. The unexplained matrix replacement does not establish a same-setting performance gain.

T1.justification: The ODE and ELBO formulations, Gaussian assumption, and edge-popup derivation in Equations 1–18 are retained. Section 4.2 cleans up the AP summation index to express the already-described all-task average. No substantive mathematical definition, assumption, theorem, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: v2 explicitly claims the first formal formulation of CDL and strengthens the introduction's characterization of regularization/replay methods as failing to alleviate forgetting in this setting. The central contributions—continual dynamics learning, MS-GODE, and a biological benchmark—and the overall effectiveness claim remain.

C2.justification: New Appendix A.1.4 attributes residual performance decline primarily to incorrect mask selection and discusses larger backbones and multiple observation splits as remedies. Sections 4.2 and 4.4 expand the pretraining limitations and parameter-overlap explanation. Conversely, v1's explicit concluding acknowledgment of the gap to joint training is removed.

D1.justification: v2 expands the brief benchmark description into detailed VCell generation instructions, script names, selected variable IDs, trajectory lengths, package versions, and example commands, and adds a code-access link. It also discloses random initialization, training task boundaries, and manual SDP tuning. The complete dataset is described as awaiting release.

R1.justification: Related work substantially expands to discuss HOPE, GG-ODE, PGODE, DIDA, CARE, and ORI, alongside additional continual-learning and pretrained dynamics-model literature. v2 more explicitly attributes its backbone to LG-ODE and discusses compatibility with irregular and incomplete observations. These additions go beyond bibliographic reformatting.

P1.justification: The abstract and introduction are extensively rewritten, CDL and Bio-CDL terminology is introduced, and the framework explanation is reorganized around backbone, subnetwork learning, and mode switching. Mask optimization and selection become separate subsections, while related-work and appendix explanations are substantially expanded.

P2.justification: v2 adds a simplified biological diagram, a phase-transition illustration, and three VCell screenshots. The original biological and physics illustrations move to appendix Figures 8 and 7. Figure 3 is revised, Figure 6 is redrawn with a shared color scale, and the document and table layout change substantially.

improvement.justification: v2 makes reproduction more actionable through its code link, generation workflow, variable lists, software versions, and execution examples, while clarifying the method's LG-ODE foundation. These gains are tempered by the unexplained replacement of Figure 6 and removal of the explicit joint-training limitation, despite Table 2 retaining AP values of 0.144 for MS-GODE versus 0.055 for Joint. The net improvement is principally in documentation and clarity.
